title: Atterbury Plot and Jacobite cipher letters (Plunket numeral cypher; numbered letters 10-19 'in cypher and French')
correspondents: Jacobite agents to Plunket, Layer, Kelly, Compton
folio_note: letters plus key leads: Plunket's numeral cypher no. 3 (35/47/52) and numerical equivalents (35/73/52)
status: Willes / Ashfield decoded much at the time; SP 35/46/47 says one paper cannot be decyphered without more text; SP 35/46/59 'Undecyphered paper'. Keys in the same volumes and BL Add MS 32256. Checked 28 Oct 2026: Dates confirmed: SP 35/45/78 (7 Oct 1723), SP 35/46/59 (c.1723, 'undecyphered'), SP 35/73/52 (Plunket numerals, c.Oct 1722). Not digitised. Keys in same volumes make this tractable. Printed-edition check, 28 Oct 2026: Partly in print. T. B. Howell, A Complete Collection of State Trials, vol. XVI (A.D. 1722-1725), Proceedings against Bishop Atterbury: Report of the Committee of the Lords on Plunkett's cypher and the numerical cypher 1378 = Atterbury ('Illington' / 'Jones'); glosses of cant names (e.g. 'barrels' = army, 'brokers' = lord Marr); decipherers' evidence incl. Mr Willes admitting that one number, 44, could not be deciphered (col. c. 506); the Bishop's defence on Plunkett's cypher (col. c. 560). The trial volume prints the committee's findings, the interpretations of cant names and the decipherers' testimony, but not the SP 35 letters as figure strings with plaintext, nor the numeral cypher tables of SP 35/47/52 or 35/73/52 as tables (glosses only). SP 35/46/59 'undecyphered paper' is not identified in it. Cruickshanks and Erskine-Hill 2004 not accessible online. OCR of the BSB scan is poor. Lead stays open for the figure-string letters; the printed glosses are a partial vocabulary for Plunket's cypher.
why: Jacobite plot ciphers with keys in the same file.
